subject: On-prem deployment: data qualification call recap & requested clarifications
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: James Huang <j.huang@aurelia.com>; Priya Sethi <priya.s@aurelia.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: On-prem deployment: data qualification call recap & requested clarifications

Hi James / Priya —

Thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap of what we captured, plus a few clarifying questions so we can scope the private/VPC deployment correctly. High level: you are evaluating a private deployment (customer-hosted data plane) with strict egress controls and an eventual need for an on-prem/air-gapped option for regulated workloads.

Summary of requirements discussed
- PII types: customer name, billing identifiers, transactional metadata, and limited health markers (flag-only).
- Retention: PII persisted for up to 7 years for transaction records; application logs retained 90 days.
- Egress: no raw PII can leave Aurelia-controlled network. Allowed: hashed identifiers, encrypted tokens, and aggregated analytics.
- Logging / audit: must provide request/response audit logs (redacted for PII) and immutable access logs for at least 12 months.
- KV cache residency: prefer caches stay entirely in customer VPC or on-prem box.

Open clarifications (can you confirm the bold items?):
1) Does the 7-year retention apply to all PII categories or only payment/transaction records? (We had mixed signals.)
2) For telemetry/logging you requested 90 days — can we confirm whether audit logs (access/elevations) should also be 12 months?
3) Network: will you provide a single CIDR block for redwood inference nodes to egress through, or do we need to support NAT + IP rotation?
4) On air-gapped option: do you need an installer that runs without internet at all, or an initial staging step is acceptable?

Attached: a draft PII mapping sheet you mentioned (aurelia_piimap.xlsx).

Next steps
- If you can confirm the three clarifications above and share the network diagram (CIDR, perimeter devices, and any required proxies), Ben will draft two deployment patterns (VPC-private data plane and on-prem airgapped) and we’ll schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive.

Availability: proposing Tue 2026-06-23 10:00 PDT or Wed 2026-06-24 14:00 PDT for the deep-dive. Please confirm.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
T: (415) 555-0182

Attachment: aurelia_piimap.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: James Huang <j.huang@aurelia.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>; Priya Sethi <priya.s@aurelia.com>
Cc: Aurelia Systems SecOps <secops@aurelia.com>
Date: 2026-06-15T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem deployment: data qualification call recap & requested clarifications

Tessa — thanks for the clear recap. A few quick answers inline and some notes from our side.

On your open clarifications:
1) The 7-year retention is specific to transaction/payment PII only (billing identifiers and transaction details). User profile PII should be retained for a maximum of 24 months unless explicitly archived.
2) Audit logs: we require access/authentication/elevation logs retained for 12 months, but operational request/response traces (full content) can be 90 days as long as PII is redacted or hashed.
3) Network: we will provide a fixed outbound NAT IP block for vendor egress. IP rotation is allowed if within that block — we do not want arbitrary external addresses.
4) Air-gap: for the highly regulated environment we need a fully air-gapped installer (no callbacks allowed). For phase 1, a staged installer with initial offline package is acceptable.

Other asks:
- Can you confirm that KV cache entries can be configured to be stored encrypted with a customer-provided KMS?
- Please share Redwood’s SOC 2 Type II report and the current retention policy template for request logs.

Attaching our network sketch that Ben asked for: aurelia_network_v1.pdf. We’ll add hostnames and device models before the tech deep-dive.

James Huang
Head of SecOps | Aurelia Systems
j.huang@aurelia.com | +1 (650) 555-2121

Attachment: aurelia_network_v1.pdf (PDF)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>; Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>; Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-16T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem deployment: data qualification call recap & requested clarifications

Thanks — capturing a proposed split of options so we can show trade-offs in the tech call. Quoted James’ notes above for context.

Option A: Customer VPC data plane (recommended for fast time-to-value)
- Control plane: Redwood managed (can be private control plane if required).
- Data plane: inference workers and KV cache run in customer VPC (private subnets).
- KV cache: persisted to an encrypted EBS volume; we can accept customer-managed KMS keys.
- Egress: all outbound traffic restricted to your NAT block; no PII payloads leave (we’ll hash/strip locally).
- Logging: request-level logs written to customer S3/log collector; redact PII before any external transmission.

Option B: On-prem / air-gapped (compliant mode)
- Installer: offline bundle that seeds images and runtime; no outbound callbacks required.
- Data residency: all artifacts (models, KV, logs) stored on customer hardware.
- Audit: local immutable logs + optional periodic signed checkpoints for attestation to Redwood (if you permit).
- Trade-offs: higher ops overhead and slower feature rollout.

Artifacts we’ll prepare for the tech deep-dive:
- Detailed dataflow diagram (redwood_private-deploy-arch.png)
- Minimal egress policy template and sample iptables/nat rules (redwood-dataflow-stub.txt)
- SOC 2 Type II summary + our control mappings (Neha to attach)

Neha — can you pull the SOC 2 summary and an example retention-policy snippet before the call? Dev — please prepare a slide showing how we handle KV cache encryption and an example of request redaction in the runtime.

If that looks good I’ll book Tue 2026-06-23 10:00 PDT for the deep-dive and block 90 minutes.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
From: Priya Sethi <priya.s@aurelia.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>; Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>; James Huang <j.huang@aurelia.com>
Date: 2026-06-17T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem deployment: data qualification call recap & requested clarifications

Ben/Tessa — appreciate the options and the write-up. Confirming next steps from Aurelia: we’ll provide an updated network diagram (adds hostnames and perimeter devices) and a redlined PII mapping by EOD Mon 2026-06-21.

We accept Option A as the initial path (customer VPC data plane) provided:
- KV cache can use customer KMS (we will supply key material and access policy).
- Audit logs for access/elevation are retained 12 months and must be exportable to our SIEM.
- For regulated tenants we need the offline installer option available in the future (phase 2).

Tech deep-dive: Tue 2026-06-23 10:00 PDT works for us. Please send calendar invite and a short pre-read (arch diagram + egress template).

Thanks —
Priya Sethi
VP, Product Security | Aurelia Systems
priya.s@aurelia.com
